# ryl

> Fast YAML linter and formatter

## Getting Started

- [Installation](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/installation/): ryl ships as a single binary. Pick the install method that matches your toolchain.
- [Shell completions](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/shell-completions/): ryl can generate tab-completion scripts for its flags. `ryl --generate-completions <SHELL>` prints the script for one shell to stdout, where `<SHELL>` is one of `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `powershell`, or `elvish`:
- [Quick Start](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/quickstart/): ryl's CLI is moving to subcommands: `ryl check` is the lint pass and `ryl format` is the formatter. `ryl check <paths>` is the recommended form and is used throughout these docs. Bare `ryl <paths>` still lints identically, but it is deprecated — it prints a warning to stderr (silenced by `--no-warnings`) and a later release will remove it, so adopt `ryl check` now.
- [Using ryl with AI agents](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/using-ryl-with-ai-agents/): ryl is built for programmatic use (stable exit codes, machine-readable output, `--fix`/`--diff`, `ryl format`, stdin), so AI coding agents can drive it directly. This page points to the agent-facing resources; the rest of these docs (start with Quick start) cover the CLI itself.
- [Migrating from yamllint](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamllint/): ryl implements yamllint's rule set, and its own configuration is TOML. ryl still reads a yamllint YAML config (`.yamllint`, `.yamllint.yml`, `.yamllint.yaml`, `-c`/`-d` YAML, `YAMLLINT_CONFIG_FILE` and the yamllint user-global config) with the same semantics as upstream, but that support is deprecated: each one prints a warning naming the command that converts it, and a later release will stop reading YAML config. Migrate with `ryl --migrate-configs`; TOML also carries the ryl-only features, such as `lint.fixable`/`lint.unfixable`.
- [Migrating from yamlfix](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamlfix/): `ryl format` covers most of yamlfix's options through `[format]` keys and the top-level `line-length` and `indent-width`. Replace `yamlfix .` with `ryl format .`, and `yamlfix --check .` with `ryl format --check .`.
- [Migrating from google/yamlfmt](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-yamlfmt/): Replace `yamlfmt .` with `ryl format .` and `yamlfmt -lint .` with `ryl format --check .`. The settings below approximate the default basic formatter in google/yamlfmt 0.21.0. They were compared on the same YAML inputs with `yamlfmt -in` and `ryl format -`.
- [Migrating from Prettier](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/getting-started/migrating-from-prettier/): For YAML files, run `ryl format .` to write changes and `ryl format --check .` in CI. Keep Prettier for other file types. The settings below follow Prettier 3.9.10's YAML output on the same inputs used with `ryl format -`. Prettier's general options can alter the starting profile.

## Configuration

- [Presets](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/config-presets/): ryl's TOML config (recommended) is the single, explicit source of a file's rules: it has no `preset` or `extends` key, inherits nothing, and merges nothing, so what it enables is the file's whole ruleset, with no default-on rules.
- [Inline directives](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/directives/): Sometimes a single line legitimately breaks a rule and changing the file is the wrong fix. ryl supports inline comment directives that switch rules off for part of a file. The preferred spelling uses `ryl`:
- [Per-line ignores](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/per-line-ignores/): Inline directives switch rules off at a specific spot in a file. `per-line-ignores` suppresses lint findings and safe `check --fix` edits on every line matching a pattern, across all files, without editing them. It is the tool for recurring exceptions &mdash; tool-directive comments and machine-managed markers that legitimately break a rule everywhere they appear.
- [File ignores](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/file-ignores/): Per-line ignores suppress rules on lines matching a pattern. This page covers the coarser layer: skipping whole files, or switching off chosen rules for a path.
- [YAML in Markdown](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/markdown/): `ryl` can lint YAML that lives **inside** Markdown documents, in addition to standalone `.yaml`/`.yml` files. Two kinds of embedded YAML are recognised:

## Other pages

- [Rules](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/rules/): ryl implements 27 rules for checking YAML files. This page is a categorised index of every rule with a brief description and a link to its detailed documentation. Each rule page covers what the rule does, why it matters, configuration options, and (where applicable) automatic fix behaviour.
- [Formatter](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/formatter/): `ryl format` rewrites YAML files in place to a consistent layout. The formatter edits only the spans that are off-style rather than reprinting the document, so the first run on an existing project produces a small diff, and every later run on formatted files changes nothing.
- [Output formats](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/output-formats/): `ryl check` renders diagnostics in several formats, selected with `--output-format` (`-f` and `--format` are aliases for `check` only). `ryl format --check` accepts `--output-format` without those aliases. The default, `auto`, picks a human-readable format for your environment; the machine-readable formats are opt-in for editors, CI, and Git forges.
- [pre-commit and prek](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/pre-commit/): ryl's hooks are published at ryl-pre-commit and run with both pre-commit and prek. Each hook installs `ryl` from PyPI at the version matching `rev`.
- [Editor integration](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/editor-integration/): `ryl server` runs ryl as a Language Server Protocol (LSP) server over stdio, so any LSP-capable editor gets ryl's diagnostics and fixes inline as you type. It is the same lint and fix engine as the CLI, exposed over the protocol.
- [YAML version compatibility](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/yaml-version/): ryl parses YAML with granit-parser (a `saphyr-parser` fork). A document with no version directive is resolved per the YAML 1.2 core schema, matching the spec, which assumes a directive-less document conforms to 1.2. Implicit type resolution can differ from tools built on YAML 1.1 loaders such as PyYAML.
- [What ryl won't do](https://ryl-docs.pages.dev/scope/): ryl lints general YAML, not the application that reads it, and its fixes never change what a document means. Requests outside that line are declined, so check this page before filing one.
